chunk_map.heading: Map the gaps, read your stack (H1/lede)
Phase 1: Diff the two runs, rank the gaps
Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule
Phase 2: Find the work you repeat across your stack
Scan your history for the work that recurs
Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams
List the checks the field runs, rank the ones that fit your gap
Route the dominant gap to its home

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.
Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 "Scan your history for the work that recurs": line 81: "> **This scan runs long, and it is yours to steer.**" — a full 9-word sentence bolded whole, not a ≲5-word handle sub-span; still present after the 2026-07-09 emphasis pass despite the maintainer note claiming blockquote callouts were left untouched as chrome (this callout is not an entry in the typed widget palette per `curriculum/widgets.md` / `site/layouts/curriculum.js` decorate* functions — it renders as plain body blockquote, so the emphasis-budget rule applies to it same as any bullet). Also chunk 7 "Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams": line 114: "> **Want to see the shapes, not read them?**" — an 8-word full question bolded whole, same violation shape. (Sibling callout at chunk 6 line 79, "**Fast operator?**", 2 words, stays within budget — not flagged.)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim both callouts' bold to a short handle span (e.g. bold just "yours to steer" / "see the shapes") and leave the rest of each sentence unbolded, or drop the bold entirely and let the blockquote carry the emphasis.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
